evidence: IDENTIFICATION DIVISION / ENVIRONMENT DIVISION / DATA DIVISION / PROCEDURE DIVISION all present
SELECT ... ASSIGN ... ORGANIZATION IS INDEXED / ACCESS MODE IS DYNAMIC / RECORD KEY / FILE STATUS
COPY ... REPLACING //token// BY //token// syntax (double-slash delimiters typical of GnuCOBOL/Micro Focus)
FD records with COPY statements for include files (.INC extension)
PIC X(nn) and PIC 9(nn) data definitions throughout
Fixed-format source with comment lines in column 7 (*)

purpose.summary: This program (ORCR1030) is part of the ORCA JMA standard medical receipt (claims) software system. It processes and edits receipt comment data for public-injury (Kouhai) receipts covering outpatient and inpatient cases. It reads, transforms, and writes indexed receipt data files (RECE100, RECE120, RECE130 series) and generates or updates comment records on medical claims.
purpose.domain: healthcare / medical billing (Japanese medical insurance claims processing)

notable_features: COPY ... REPLACING with double-slash delimiter syntax (GnuCOBOL/Micro Focus style)
Multiple indexed VSAM-style files with DYNAMIC access mode
Large working-storage with many flag (FLG-*), counter (CNT-*), and index (IDX-*) areas
Japanese-language comments encoded in Latin-1 (actually EUC-JP or Shift-JIS rendered as Latin-1)
No EXEC SQL or EXEC CICS — pure file-based batch processing
45 CALL statements and 799 PERFORM statements indicating a large, modular batch program
Error file (RECEERR-FILE) for logging processing errors
Extensive revision history in comments spanning 2007–2016
verdict.notes: The file is decoded as Latin-1 but the Japanese comments are almost certainly EUC-JP or Shift-JIS, causing mojibake in the displayed text. The COPY statements reference external .INC copybooks that are not shown. The double-slash REPLACING delimiter is characteristic of GnuCOBOL or Micro Focus rather than IBM Enterprise COBOL. The program is part of the well-known open-source ORCA medical claims system developed by JMA (Japan Medical Association). Source is truncated at 16000 chars out of ~402KB total.
